title: The card is not dead until you write to it

sources.name: GNU ddrescue manual — 'Important advice' and the option list
quoted: Never try to rescue a r/w mounted partition.
It is best that the device or partition to be rescued is not mounted at all, not even read-only.
Never try to repair a file system on a drive with I/O errors; you will probably lose even more data.
If you use a device or a partition as destination, any data stored there will be overwritten.
The mapfile is an essential part of ddrescue's effectiveness. Use it unless you know what you are doing.
Also you may interrupt the rescue at any time and resume it later at the same point.

sources.name: CGSecurity — PhotoRec (project page and 'How PhotoRec works')
quoted: PhotoRec ignores the file system; this way it works even if the file system is severely damaged.

As soon as a picture or file is accidentally deleted, or you discover any missing, do NOT save any more pictures or files to that memory device or hard disk drive; otherwise you may overwrite your lost data.
while using PhotoRec, you must not choose to write the recovered files to the same partition they were stored on
